claims.claim: On addition, mean final held-out CE is 339.459 without decay versus 8.390 with decay at width 16, and 89.877 versus 8.627 at width 256. Loss differences do not establish generalization events or a mechanism.

The three-seed mean initial parameter norms are 6.288, 7.383, and 10.904 at widths 16, 64, and 256. Initial norms coincide across operation/decay arms at fixed width and seed, but widths are not norm-matched.
The final factorial contains addition and subtraction modulo 97, widths 16, 64, and 256, decay 0 and 1, and initialization seeds 1009, 2027, and 3037, for 36 completed records.
Thirty records attain sustained memorization and zero attain sustained generalization by 20,000 updates; none of the 30 fitted records has an observed delayed-generalization event.

Each operation enumerates 9409 pairs and retains 4705 in the final partition, with 1411 training and 3294 held-out examples; approximately 30% of the final subset and 15% of the full universe train the network.
claims.derivation: Read p=97 in evaluated source; count retained resource examples by split; compute p squared and split fractions. Episode parameter counts and traces identify the evaluated family.

claims.claim: The input concatenates two one-hot vectors into 194 dimensions; the classifier has a ReLU hidden layer of width w, biases in both linear layers, and 97 output logits, with 292w+97 parameters.
Widths 16, 64, and 256 have 4769, 18785, and 74849 trainable parameters, respectively, and use default PyTorch linear initialization without logit-scale matching.
Training uses full-batch cross-entropy and AdamW with shared constant learning rate 0.01, decay 0 or 1, betas 0.9 and 0.999, epsilon 1e-8, and no bias-specific parameter groups.

The protocol runs 20000 updates per condition with measurements at initialization and every 500 updates, using deterministic algorithms and a single compute/interoperation thread; each condition resets training state.
The original neural-training dependencies are numpy==2.1.3 and torch==2.5.1+cpu.

Memorization requires at least 99% training accuracy for three consecutive checkpoints, and generalization requires at least 95% held-out accuracy for three consecutive checkpoints; event timestamps are window starts.
Late-window accuracies average the final five checkpoints, covering updates 18000 through 20000, independently of the sustained-event test.

Without decay all widths memorize: width 16 at 1000 to 1500 updates and widths 64 and 256 at 500 updates across operations and seeds. The exact twelve condition rows and seed times appear in the main event table.
With positive decay all six width-16 records fail to memorize by the horizon, whereas all width-64 and width-256 records memorize at 500 updates.
All zero-decay late-window training accuracies average 100%; with positive decay width-16 means are 56.664% for addition and 55.625% for subtraction, while all wider conditions average 100%.

Zero-decay width-16 held-out seed means and sample standard deviations are 0.482 +/- 0.061% for addition and 0.407 +/- 0.006% for subtraction; width-64 means are 0.047% and 0.026%; width-256 late-window accuracy is zero in every seed.
Positive-decay held-out means for widths 16,64,256 are 0.219%,0.091%,0.091% on addition and 0.178%,0.053%,0.117% on subtraction; these low values do not support a common monotone width trend.
The overall late-window held-out mean is 0.142515%, averaging all 36 conditions equally rather than filtering on fitting attainment.

Mode, lookup-fallback, deranged-alignment, and initialized-network reference means are respectively 0.865209%,0.865209%,0.949201%,1.050732%; the trained-minus-reference mean gap is -0.790073 percentage points.
The lookup and mode references coincide because held-out input pairs are disjoint from the training lookup; deranged alignment is not independently randomized-label training.
The lag substitutes H for unobserved generalization, uses H-T_M for observed memorization with unobserved generalization, and assigns H when memorization is not observed.

At positive decay, width-16 capped lag is 20000 and width-256 capped lag is 19500; every paired seed contrast is 500, with the supplied interval [500,500]. This is not an observed generalization-time contrast.
Zero-decay operation-averaged seed contrasts are -750,-500,-500, with mean -583.333; the difference of mean contrasts across decay arms is 1083.333 updates.
The mean capped lag over all records is 19486.111 updates, not a mean uncensored grokking delay.
The supplied interval uses the sample standard deviation of three paired contrasts and multiplier 4.30265273/sqrt(3), clipped to [-H,H]; its degeneracy follows from zero contrast variation.

The supplementary table preserves all 36 records' event times, capped lags, and final-five-checkpoint accuracies; the diagnostic table averages final-checkpoint training CE, held-out CE, and parameter norm over the three seeds for each condition.
The three stored seed-evaluation durations, each covering its condition grid, are 786.393,777.546,786.875 seconds; they are observations, not portable runtime guarantees.

The independent final qualification sources report completed, qualified, and true; this acceptance does not establish generalization or a neural mechanism. The retained diagnostics-trust designation is unverified.

No matched final-plane comparison to the original lower-rate recipe is retained; development scores are not used as final results, and no cross-task transfer, random-label training, initial-logit calibration, circuit measurement, or generalization-time equivalence is claimed.
The final evaluator and observation-file hashes match their final metadata; hashes identify supplied artifacts rather than prove implementation substance.
Grokking can produce held-out improvement long after training-set fitting on small algorithmic datasets, with dataset size affecting optimization requirements.
AdamW decouples weight decay from the loss-gradient update; the fixed-rate shrinkage contribution (1-eta*lambda)^t is not the full trained parameter trajectory.
Omnigrok discusses weight-norm loss landscapes and grokking beyond algorithmic data; those mechanisms are comparator context, not measured conclusions of this study.
Circuit efficiency proposes competition between memorizing and generalizing solutions with different learning speeds and norm efficiency; the present experiment does not measure that mechanism.
Lazy-to-rich dynamics is an analyzed grokking account including a two-layer polynomial-regression setting; no kernel or feature-learning diagnostic is measured here.
Unifying Grokking and Double Descent proposes a pattern-learning-speed account including variation in model capacity; this work does not establish double descent.
Deep Double Descent reports nonmonotone performance with model size and training duration in other settings; the present sparse grid does not infer a general width law.
Fitting labels and explaining generalization are distinct problems, as illustrated by random-label fitting results in the cited literature, not independently executed in this study.
LLMs contributed to proposals, bounded controller implementation, query planning, framing, analysis code, writing and grounding; the training computation owns the retained numerical observations.
